question: A 22-year-old primigravida is admitted to the obstetrics ward with leg swelling at 35 weeks gestation. She denies any other symptoms. Her pregnancy has been uneventful and she was compliant with the recommended prenatal care. Her vital signs were as follows: blood pressure, 168/95 mm Hg; heart rate, 86/min; respiratory rate, 16/min; and temperature, 36.7℃ (98℉). The fetal heart rate was 141/min. The physical examination was significant for 2+ pitting edema of the lower extremity. A dipstick test shows 1+ proteinuria. On reassessment 15 minutes later without administration of an antihypertensive, her blood pressure was 141/88 mm Hg, and the fetal heart rate was 147/min. A decision was made to observe the patient and continue the work-up without initiating antihypertensive therapy. Which of the following clinical features would make the suspected diagnosis into a more severe form?

options.opb: Blood pressure of 165/90 mm Hg reassessed 4 hours later

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Primigravida at 35 weeks gestation" -> "Leg swelling" -> "Pitting edema of lower extremities" -> "1+ proteinuria" -> "Blood pressure 168/95 mm Hg" -> "Fetal heart rate 141/min" -> "Pre-eclampsia suspicion" -> 70% CHAIN: "Pre-eclampsia suspicion" -> "Blood pressure 141/88 mm Hg after 15 minutes" -> "Fetal heart rate 147/min" -> "Observation without antihypertensive therapy" -> 60% CHAIN: "Observation without antihypertensive therapy" -> "Clinical features worsening pre-eclampsia" -> 40% CHAIN: "Clinical features worsening pre-eclampsia" -> "24-hour urinary protein of 5 g/L" -> "Severe pre-eclampsia" -> 80% CHAIN: "Clinical features worsening pre-eclampsia" -> "Blood pressure of 165/90 mm Hg reassessed 4 hours later" -> "Severe pre-eclampsia" -> 75% CHAIN: "Clinical features worsening pre-eclampsia" -> "Hematocrit of 0.55" -> "Severe pre-eclampsia" -> 70% CHAIN: "Clinical features worsening pre-eclampsia" -> "Platelet count 133,000/μL" -> "Severe pre-eclampsia" -> 70% CHAIN: "Clinical features worsening pre-eclampsia" -> "Serum creatinine 0.98 mg/dL" -> "Severe pre-eclampsia" -> 70%
enhanced_information: Clinical features that would make the suspected diagnosis of pre-eclampsia more severe include a 24-hour urinary protein of 5 g/L, a blood pressure of 165/90 mm Hg reassessed 4 hours later, a hematocrit of 0.55, a platelet count of 133,000/μL, and a serum creatinine of 0.98 mg/dL. These parameters indicate progression to severe pre-eclampsia.
analysis: The clinical scenario suggests a case of preeclampsia, characterized by hypertension and proteinuria after 20 weeks of gestation. Severe features of preeclampsia include severe hypertension (≥160/110 mm Hg), thrombocytopenia (platelet count <100,000/μL), impaired liver function, renal insufficiency, pulmonary edema, or new-onset cerebral or visual disturbances. Among the options, a platelet count of 133,000/μL indicates thrombocytopenia, which is a feature of severe preeclampsia. The other options do not meet the criteria for severe features: 24-hour urinary protein of 5 g/L indicates significant proteinuria but not necessarily severe preeclampsia; a blood pressure of 165/90 mm Hg is elevated but not in the severe range; a hematocrit of 0.55 is high but not a direct indicator of severe preeclampsia; and a serum creatinine of 0.98 mg/dL is within normal limits.
